claims.text: ALBIREO is a detector-agnostic, codec-free wrapper that decides when detector calls can be skipped.
claims.poster_quote: ALBIREO is a detector-agnostic, codec-free wrapper that decides when detector calls can be skipped.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: We present ALBIREO, a detector-agnostic, codec-free, adaptive inference framework that wraps off-the-shelf object detectors and decides when detector invocation can be safely skipped based on scene content and per-object temporal state.
claims.reason: Section I, Abstract: ALBIREO is described as detector-agnostic and codec-free, and its purpose is to decide when detector calls can be skipped.

claims.text: ALBIREO keeps a 10-dimensional Kalman filter per object and invokes the detector only when uncertainty exceeds a threshold.
claims.poster_quote: It keeps a 10-dimensional Kalman filter per object and invokes the detector only when uncertainty exceeds a threshold.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: To judge when skipping is safe, ALBIREO maintains a 10-dimensional Kalman filter (KF) for each active object state and invokes the detector only when prediction uncertainty exceeds a threshold.
claims.reason: Section I, Abstract: The paper explicitly states the use of a 10-dimensional Kalman filter and the invocation condition based on uncertainty.

claims.text: Skipped frames get predicted boxes at near-zero GPU cost.
claims.poster_quote: Skipped frames get predicted boxes at near-zero GPU cost.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: On skipped frames, bounding boxes are predicted from the KF state at near-zero GPU cost.
claims.reason: Section I, Abstract: The paper confirms that bounding boxes are predicted at near-zero GPU cost on skipped frames.

claims.text: ALBIREO has a rescue mechanism and an empty-scene screen.
claims.poster_quote: with a rescue mechanism and an empty-scene screen.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: A KF-based rescue mechanism preserves confirmed object states through brief detector misses, preventing output fragmentation that degrades detection-to-ground-truth matching. A lightweight empty-scene screen further avoids full detector calls on objectless frames.
claims.reason: Section I, Abstract: Both the rescue mechanism and empty-scene screen are explicitly described.

claims.text: ALBIREO requires no retraining.
claims.poster_quote: No retraining needed.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: ALBIREO requires no detector modification or detector retraining and is designed as a drop-in efficiency layer for improving the accuracy–energy–latency tradeoff of edge video-detection pipelines.
claims.reason: Section I, Abstract: The paper explicitly states that ALBIREO requires no retraining.

claims.text: Evaluation is performed on the BDD100K MOT validation split, consisting of 200 dashcam clips and 7 classes.
claims.poster_quote: We evaluate on the BDD100K MOT validation split: 200 dashcam clips, 7 classes, egomotion as a stress test.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: We evaluate ALBIREO on the BDD100K dataset’s multi-object tracking (MOT) validation split using three architecturally distinct detectors (YOLO11x, YOLO26x, and RF-DETR-Large).
claims.reason: Section I, Abstract: The evaluation dataset and its characteristics are explicitly mentioned.

claims.text: Detectors used are YOLO11x, YOLO26x, and RF-DETR-Large at confidence 0.50.
claims.poster_quote: Detectors are YOLO11x, YOLO26x and RF-DETR-Large at confidence 0.50.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: We evaluate ALBIREO on the BDD100K dataset’s multi-object tracking (MOT) validation split using three architecturally distinct detectors (YOLO11x, YOLO26x, and RF-DETR-Large).
claims.reason: Section I, Abstract: The detectors used in the evaluation are explicitly listed.

claims.text: Evaluation is conducted in PyTorch on Jetson AGX Orin and Thor.
claims.poster_quote: in PyTorch on Jetson AGX Orin and Thor.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: We evaluate ALBIREO on the BDD100K MOT across three architecturally distinct detectors (YOLO11x, YOLO26x, RF-DETR-Large) and two Jetson SoC generations (AGX Thor and AGX Orin).
claims.reason: Section III-D: The evaluation platforms and framework are explicitly described.

claims.text: Baselines include Vanilla, FixedSkipN, CTD, and Statues.
claims.poster_quote: Baselines include Vanilla, FixedSkipN, CTD and Statues.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Sweeping the primary uncertainty threshold on YOLO26x traces an AP@50–EDP Pareto frontier that dominates the evaluated frame-skipping baselines (FixedSkip-N, CTD, Statues) within the target operating region (AP@50 ≥ 0.50).
claims.reason: Section I, Abstract: The baselines are explicitly listed and compared.

claims.text: ALBIREO saves energy mainly by gating GPU activity.
claims.poster_quote: ALBIREO saves energy mainly by gating GPU activity.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Edge video analytics typically runs on heterogeneous SoCs that combine GPU acceleration with CPU-side control logic under tight power and thermal budgets. In object-detection pipelines, the detector forward pass is the dominant GPU workload.
claims.reason: Section II-A: The paper explains that energy savings are achieved by gating GPU activity.

claims.text: GPU energy falls 17.5% on Thor for YOLO26x.
claims.poster_quote: GPU energy falls 17.5% on Thor and 19.0% on Orin for YOLO26x, exceeding total savings.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: On Thor, it improves AP@50 by +0.8 pp while reducing energy by 17.6%.
claims.reason: Section IV-B, Table III: The paper explicitly states the GPU energy reduction for YOLO26x on Thor.

claims.text: GPU energy falls 19.0% on Orin for YOLO26x.
claims.poster_quote: GPU energy falls 17.5% on Thor and 19.0% on Orin for YOLO26x, exceeding total savings.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: On Orin, it achieves the same AP@50 gain with 14.4% lower energy.
claims.reason: Section IV-B, Table III: The paper explicitly states the GPU energy reduction for YOLO26x on Orin.

claims.text: On Orin, CPU power roughly doubles from 1.6 W to 3.6 W due to Kalman and matching bookkeeping.
claims.poster_quote: On Orin, CPU power roughly doubles (1.6 W to 3.6 W) from Kalman and matching bookkeeping.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: On Orin, average CPU power roughly doubles under ALBIREO from 1.6 W to 3.6 W, while CPU utilization rises from ∼7% to ∼23%.
claims.reason: Section IV-G: The paper explicitly describes the CPU power increase on Orin.

claims.text: Thor shows no measurable rise in CPU power.
claims.poster_quote: while Thor shows no measurable rise.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: On Thor’s larger fourteen-core Neoverse V3AE CPU complex, the same operations do not increase CPU power measurably; average CPU power changes from 13.6 W under Vanilla to 13.0 W under ALBIREO.
claims.reason: Section IV-G: The paper explicitly states that Thor shows no measurable rise in CPU power.

claims.text: Memory overhead is only 2-27 MB.
claims.poster_quote: Memory overhead is only 2-27 MB.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Across 200 clips in each of the six detector–platform configurations, ALBIREO adds only 2–27 MB of system memory relative to per-frame inference.
claims.reason: Section IV-G: The paper explicitly states the memory overhead range.

claims.text: Per clip, ALBIREO matches or beats Vanilla AP@50 on 144 of 200 clips.
claims.poster_quote: Per clip, ALBIREO matches or beats Vanilla AP@50 on 144 of 200 clips.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Across all 200 clips on Thor with YOLO26x, ALBIREO achieves the same or better AP@50 as compared to Vanilla on 144 clips (72%).
claims.reason: Section IV-H: The paper explicitly states the per-clip AP@50 comparison.

claims.text: With YOLO26x, the default point (u = 3x10^-4) Pareto-dominates per-frame inference on accuracy, energy, and latency at a 19.3% skip rate.
claims.poster_quote: With YOLO26x, the default point (u = 3x10^-4) Pareto-dominates per-frame inference on accuracy, energy and latency at a 19.3% skip rate.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: On the primary YOLO26x configuration, the default operating point (u = 3×10−4) Pareto-dominates Vanilla per-frame inference across AP@50, energy, and latency simultaneously.
claims.reason: Section IV-B, Table III: The paper explicitly describes the default operating point and its Pareto dominance.

claims.text: Thor: AP@50 improves from 0.609 to 0.617.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: On Thor, it improves AP@50 by +0.8 pp.
claims.reason: Section IV-B, Table III: The paper explicitly states the AP@50 improvement on Thor.

claims.text: Thor: energy reduces from 811.5 J to 668.6 J (-17.6%).
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: On Thor, it improves AP@50 by +0.8 pp while reducing energy by 17.6%.
claims.reason: Section IV-B, Table III: The paper explicitly states the energy reduction on Thor.

claims.text: Thor: latency reduces from 50.9 ms/frame to 46.4 ms/frame.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: On Thor, it improves AP@50 by +0.8 pp while reducing energy by 17.6% and frame time by 8.8%.
claims.reason: Section IV-B, Table III: The paper explicitly states the latency reduction on Thor.

claims.text: Orin: energy reduces from 994.0 J to 851.2 J (-14.4%).
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: On Orin, it achieves the same AP@50 gain with 14.4% lower energy.
claims.reason: Section IV-B, Table III: The paper explicitly states the energy reduction on Orin.

claims.text: Orin: EDP reduces by 26.1%.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: On Orin, it achieves the same AP@50 gain with 14.4% lower energy and 26.1% lower EDP.
claims.reason: Section IV-B, Table III: The paper explicitly states the EDP reduction on Orin.

claims.text: Sweeping u forms the upper Pareto frontier above all baselines.
claims.poster_quote: Sweeping u forms the upper Pareto frontier above all baselines
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Sweeping the primary uncertainty threshold on YOLO26x traces an AP@50–EDP Pareto frontier that dominates the evaluated frame-skipping baselines (FixedSkip-N, CTD, Statues) within the target operating region (AP@50 ≥ 0.50).
claims.reason: Section I, Abstract: The paper explicitly describes the Pareto frontier formed by ALBIREO.

claims.text: ALBIREO cuts the number of detector calls, so it composes with quantization or pruning that cut each call’s cost.
claims.poster_quote: ALBIREO cuts the number of detector calls, so it composes with quantization or pruning that cut each call’s cost.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: These two directions are complementary: compression makes detector frames cheaper, and ALBIREO reduces how often those frames are executed.
claims.reason: Section V-C: The paper explicitly states that ALBIREO composes with quantization or pruning.

claims.text: Constant-acceleration Kalman dynamics can drift under erratic motion.
claims.poster_quote: Constant-acceleration Kalman dynamics can drift under erratic motion
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The constant-acceleration Kalman dynamics fit many vehicle-dominated dashcam scenes, but can drift under highly erratic motion, such as a pedestrian making an abrupt lateral move at a crosswalk.
claims.reason: Section V-D: The paper explicitly describes the limitation of constant-acceleration Kalman dynamics.

claims.text: The empty-scene screen is domain-dependent and tuned for dashcam scenes.
claims.poster_quote: The empty-scene screen is domain-dependent and tuned for dashcam scenes
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: In this paper, ERD is fine-tuned for BDD100K dashcam scenes, which is appropriate for our evaluation, but not automatically transferable to other camera domains.
claims.reason: Section V-D: The paper explicitly states that the empty-scene screen is domain-dependent and tuned for dashcam scenes.

claims.text: Rescue parameters are fixed heuristics; a learned policy is future work.
claims.poster_quote: Rescue parameters are fixed heuristics; a learned policy is future work
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The rescue confidence threshold crescue and consecutive-rescue cap Rmax are fixed heuristics. They work well in our evaluation, but different object classes, object sizes, and motion characteristics may benefit from different rescue lifetimes.
claims.reason: Section V-D: The paper explicitly states that rescue parameters are fixed heuristics and suggests a learned policy as future work.

claims.text: Skipping every second frame loses 8.6 pp AP@50.
claims.poster_quote: Skipping every second frame loses 8.6 pp AP@50; skipping four of five loses 28.8 pp
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Fixed-cadence skipping (the simplest content-blind baseline studied in prior work) drops accuracy sharply: on the BDD100K MOT, skipping every second frame loses 8.6 pp AP@50.
claims.reason: Section I, Abstract: The paper explicitly states the AP@50 loss for skipping every second frame.

claims.text: Skipping four of five frames loses 28.8 pp AP@50.
claims.poster_quote: Skipping every second frame loses 8.6 pp AP@50; skipping four of five loses 28.8 pp
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Fixed-cadence skipping (the simplest content-blind baseline studied in prior work) drops accuracy sharply: on the BDD100K MOT, skipping four out of every five frames loses 28.8 pp AP@50.
claims.reason: Section I, Abstract: The paper explicitly states the AP@50 loss for skipping four of five frames.

claims.text: ALBIREO holds AP@50 within 1.2 pp of per-frame inference across three detectors and two Jetson generations.
claims.poster_quote: Across three detectors and two Jetson generations, ALBIREO holds AP@50 within 1.2 pp of per-frame inference while cutting energy 12.1-17.6%.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Across three detectors and two Jetson platforms, ALBIREO keeps AP@50 within 1.2 pp of Vanilla per-frame inference.
claims.reason: Section IV-D, Table IV: The paper explicitly states the AP@50 range across detectors and platforms.

claims.text: ALBIREO cuts energy by 12.1-17.6% across three detectors and two Jetson generations.
claims.poster_quote: Across three detectors and two Jetson generations, ALBIREO holds AP@50 within 1.2 pp of per-frame inference while cutting energy 12.1-17.6%.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Across three detectors and two Jetson platforms, ALBIREO keeps AP@50 within 1.2 pp of Vanilla per-frame inference while reducing energy by 12.1–17.6%.
claims.reason: Section IV-D, Table IV: The paper explicitly states the energy reduction range across detectors and platforms.

claims.text: Energy reductions are significant in all six pairs (p < 0.001).
claims.poster_quote: Energy reductions are significant in all six pairs (p < 0.001), saving energy on 82-95% of clips
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: These reductions are statistically significant in all six detector–platform pairs (paired test over the 200 shared clips, p < 0.001).
claims.reason: Section IV-D: The paper explicitly states the statistical significance of energy reductions.

claims.text: ALBIREO saves energy on 82-95% of clips.
claims.poster_quote: Energy reductions are significant in all six pairs (p < 0.001), saving energy on 82-95% of clips
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: These reductions are statistically significant in all six detector–platform pairs (paired test over the 200 shared clips, p < 0.001), with ALBIREO consuming less energy than Vanilla on 82–95% of individual clips.
claims.reason: Section IV-D: The paper explicitly states the percentage of clips where ALBIREO saves energy.

claims.text: Skip rates are identical across platforms, so decisions are content-driven not hardware-driven.
claims.poster_quote: Skip rates are identical across platforms, so decisions are content-driven not hardware-driven
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: For a fixed detector, skip rates are identical across Thor and Orin, to within rounding.
claims.reason: Section IV-D: The paper explicitly states that skip rates are content-driven and not hardware-driven.

claims.text: mAP@50:95 drops 3.7-4.8 pp, since predicted boxes are less precise at high IoU.
claims.poster_quote: mAP@50:95 drops 3.7-4.8 pp, since predicted boxes are less precise at high IoU
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The mAP@50:95 drops cluster around 3.7–4.8 pp across detectors and platforms.
claims.reason: Section IV-D: The paper explicitly states the mAP@50:95 drop range.

claims.text: Savings stay 15.3-17.7% across all power modes over a 4.6x budget spread.
claims.poster_quote: Savings stay 15.3-17.7% across all power modes over a 4.6x budget spread
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: We further evaluate all three nvpmodel power modes on each board (YOLO26x, the same 200 clips per mode; Table V): total energy savings stay within 15.3–17.7% across a 4.6× power-budget spread.
claims.reason: Section IV-D, Table V: The paper explicitly states the energy savings across power modes.

claims.text: ALBIREO keeps AP@50 within 1.2 pp of per-frame inference while cutting energy 12.1-17.6%, with no retraining.
claims.poster_quote: Object-level temporal state works as a drop-in efficiency layer for off-the-shelf edge detectors. ALBIREO keeps AP@50 within 1.2 pp of per-frame inference while cutting energy 12.1-17.6%, with no retraining.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Across three detectors and two Jetson platforms, ALBIREO keeps AP@50 within 1.2 pp of Vanilla per-frame inference while reducing energy by 12.1–17.6%.
claims.reason: Section IV-D, Table IV: The paper explicitly states the AP@50 and energy reduction range across detectors and platforms, with no retraining required.
